blocks.x: Well, Paul Barberin used to tell me that Joe Glazer had some white arrangers.
He had some white arrangers also. I'm forgetting the name. No.
Joe Glazer took the band over.
That's when Russell lost the band. Joe Glazer took over. I guess he made big money. He did.
He made millions for Joe. We knew he made millions for Joe Glazer.

When Joe Glazer came with Louis, he was a big show. He had nothing. Louis just had the trumpet. Joe Glazer had that one suit. I remember that. He was hustling. He started booking the band. He had a little piece. Mills had an office. Joe Glazer had a little corner where he used to get the ring. The next year, Joe Glazer had an office in Radio City. One office. He was a multimillionaire when he died. Did you make any movies, by the way? We made one in New York. That was with a singer, Martin Donnelly. You know Martin Donnelly? I know who you're talking about. In fact, that was something I can just talk about. He had a very nice tenor voice, Irishman. We made this in New York. This was around 1934 or 1933 in Long Island. It was a deal of the movie. It was a lot of plot to the picture. I saw the picture after. We had a little point in it. It was like a music store. Russell comes in. He's a talkie. He said, Hey, that's where it's Russell. Why don't you join us and do something. He said, Mr. Donnelly is here. Why don't you play it now? We played one number for him.
